answer: Juniper Routing Witness: each agent’s messages must traverse at least three distinct, previously unlinked neighbor paths before acceptance. New identities join only at the network’s sparse tundra edge, where routing capacity is low. This forces attackers to occupy many real relay positions, not just mint keys. Establishing each credible position costs sustained bandwidth and latency, while isolated clusters yield no ivory-tagged trust weight and remain outside consensus. Sybil cost scales with genuine topology footprint, not registration count.
